executive_assessment.text: The NDC says coastal and marine ecosystems face storms, flooding, erosion and sea-level rise, with growing freshwater scarcity and declining marine productivity.
NC4 identifies vulnerabilities in coastal, Bijagós, inland agricultural, and riverside areas, linked to poverty, natural-resource dependence, and institutional and infrastructure weaknesses.
The NDC proposes 50 km of coastal and riverine anti-salt dykes by 2035, prioritizing high-risk areas with predominantly women residents; mangrove restoration is also targeted.

geographic_notes.text: Coastal and riverine high-risk areas of Guinea-Bissau: The NDC proposes 50 km of coastal and riverine anti-salt dykes by 2035, prioritizing high-risk areas with predominantly women residents; mangrove restoration is also targeted.

Coastal areas; Bijagós Archipelago; Inland agricultural areas; Riverside communities: NC4 identifies vulnerabilities in coastal, Bijagós, inland agricultural, and riverside areas, linked to poverty, natural-resource dependence, and institutional and infrastructure weaknesses.

Coastal communities; Agricultural areas; Bijagós Archipelago: NC4 reports coastal displacement from land and housing loss, farmer crop failures amid unpredictable rainfall, and threats to Bijagós ecosystems.

Coastal zone; Interior; Southwest; Bijagós Archipelago: For 2016–2045, the NDC projects coastal warming of 1.2°C under RCP4.5 and 1.3°C under RCP8.5, versus 1.4°C and 1.5°C inland; rainfall is projected to rise slightly or stagnate, with local exceptions.

Interior; Coastal zone; Bissau: The NDC describes the interior as prone to longer droughts, fires, floods, and water shortages; the coastal zone holds about 70% of the population and faces saline intrusion in agricultural fields.

known_gaps.text: NC4 explicitly reserves all rights and requires prior authorization; only original paraphrases, not source text, are recorded.
The 2026 NDC PDF labels itself draft even though the UNFCCC registry marks the submission active.
The earlier NDC uses a different coastal-zone estimate than NDC 3.0; its projection and population figures are kept source-specific rather than combined.
